key_insight: Distal weight-bearing implants work as a coupled mechanical-biological system, where geometry, graded biomaterial interfaces, and gait-phase loading together determine fixation durability and osseointegration.
engineering_relevance: For transfemoral implant design, the main challenge is balancing distal support with lower bending moments, controlled micromotion, coating integrity, and long-term bone-implant integration.
method: Systematic review of DWBI design, biomaterials, and translation pathways
Trend analysis of 34 direct-contribution papers and 32 empirical studies
Synthesis of finite element analysis, FGM/Ti-HAp architectures, and in-vivo evidence
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that more than half of the empirical evidence remained at bench or simulation level, with animal and clinical studies forming a smaller validation layer.
watch_item: Graded Ti-HAp and FGM concepts are still supported mainly by non-DWBI analog studies, so device-specific validation and fatigue/coating testing remain necessary.
paper_title: Biomaterials and biomechanical design of distal weight-bearing implants: Computational modeling, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation
